The article title is misleading. Not only does the article specifically say that Win 10 share probably did not drop, the Steam percentages are not a good measure of platform usage. Because the Steam figures are released only as percentages, a drop in percentage (or an increase or a staying-the-same) indicates only that change in relation to all other platforms. So, for instance, Win 10 usage could theoretically have increased by several tens of thousands (or any amount) and still show the reported change in percentage if the other platforms increased at a similar rate. The published statistics tell us that primarily that of all the users of Steam, slightly less than half of them are Windows 10 users. They don't tell us how many people are using any of the platforms.

In order for the article to be correct, we would have to 1) see a decrease in the overall Win 10 percentage, 2) see rise in percentage for other platforms, 3) and know the amount of increase or decrease of total Steam users. Since we only see 1 (maybe) & 2 but don't know 3, we cannot say with certainty that Windows 10 usage is dropping.

All of that and I still find this to be really good news! As of the time of this writing, the Steam survey results show a small but decided decrease in Win 10 percentage and a small but across the board increase in Linux percentage. Go team Penguin!
